 Kenyans face earlier KRA tax filing deadline for individuals
 Sacco Review November 15, 2026 0 5 mins 
 KRA is introducing an earlier deadline for individual income tax returns. 
 Taxpayers will have less time to prepare and submit annual returns. 
 Employers and individuals face new pressure to organise tax records early. 
 Kenyans will have to adjust their tax compliance routines after the Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) brought forward the deadline for filing individual income tax returns by two months.
 The revised timeline takes effect on January 1, 2027, requiring taxpayers to submit their 2026 income tax returns by April 30, 2027, instead of the traditional June 30 deadline.
 The change means individuals, salaried employees, business owners and other taxpayers will have less time to prepare and submit their annual returns, placing greater emphasis on timely record-keeping and early compliance.
 For years, many taxpayers have waited until June to gather the documents required for filing, often leading to last-minute pressure, errors and delays.
 However, the earlier deadline is expected to challenge this culture, forcing individuals to take a more organised approach to managing their tax records throughout the year.
 Although employers deduct Pay As You Earn (PAYE) from employees’ monthly salaries, workers are still required to ensure their annual returns are accurately completed and submitted to KRA.
 Taxpayers must therefore verify their employment income details, tax deductions and other relevant information before submitting their returns.

 KRA promises easier tax compliance through prefilled returns 
 Those earning income from businesses, freelance assignments, rental properties and other sources will also need to maintain proper financial records to avoid omissions and discrepancies.
 The shortened filing period could particularly affect individuals who wait until the final weeks to retrieve employment documents, reconcile their income or seek assistance with tax-related queries.
 KRA will also face the task of ensuring taxpayers understand the revised requirements before the new deadline takes effect.
 Clear public communication will be necessary to help individuals establish who is required to file, the documents needed and the procedures for correcting errors in their returns.
 Employers will equally have a role to play by ensuring workers receive relevant tax documents in good time to facilitate compliance.
 Taxpayers have been encouraged to begin preparing their 2026 financial records early rather than waiting until April to establish their filing obligations.
 The new timeline is expected to test both taxpayer awareness and preparedness as the authority seeks to strengthen compliance.
 With April 30, 2027, replacing June 30 as the filing deadline for 2026 individual income tax returns, Kenyans will need to abandon the traditional last-minute rush and make tax compliance a year-round responsibility.
 By Kimwele Mutuku
